hypothesis: A should receive 5. B tests whether a related but unsupported additional diagnosis is accepted as fully correct. No unique lower score is pre-assigned to B, because the rubric's explicit 3-point addition rule says incorrect AND unrelated.
primary_measure: B receiving score 5 despite the unsupported addition
manual_evidence_review: Case narrative and all 54 saved question/test results reviewed before outcome inspection.
No hypogammaglobulinemia diagnosis or quantitative total IgG/IgA/IgM result is supplied.
Reported pathogen-specific IgG/IgM and antiphospholipid antibodies are not quantitative total immunoglobulin measurements.
SPEP/immunofixation says no monoclonal protein; no decreased gamma fraction or total Ig level is reported.
This is an unsupported addition, not proof of biological impossibility or an observed diagnostic-agent error.
relatedness_note: Published IVLBCL cohort reports hypogammaglobulinemia among hemophagocytic-variant features. This motivates a related clinical addition, not evidence that the synthetic patient has it. Source NOT sent to Judge.
sampling_note: No temperature or seed sent to API. Fresh isolated calls. Fixed local seed only shuffles call order.
operational_settings: 16384 combined output/reasoning token cap; parameter-support-required routing; ZDR/data_collection deny; no pro mode; no extra judge instructions or A/B labels.
limitations: Single synthetic case and single preselected perturbation; three repetitions are exploratory.
GPT-5 and Astra differ in both model and reasoning setting; not a model-only causal comparison.
Saved GPT-5 Gatekeeper results are fixed context; no Astra diagnostic rollout is tested.
Raw evidence and qualitative review do not establish clinical gold labels for every possible score.
